title: Manifest diffing between snapshots (foundational)
description: Two manifest snapshots are diffed by database identifier, classifying each entry as added, removed, or changed. Diffing is set-based and runs in linear time, so even hundred-thousand-entry manifests compare quickly. The diff is the raw material for every expansion finding. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Archive Expansion Detector practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: New-database detection with metadata fetch (foundational)
description: Each added identifier triggers a metadata fetch: name, record count, categories, and provenance. Metadata turns a bare 'new id' into a useful expansion record. Databases whose metadata cannot be fetched are flagged as unreachable rather than silently skipped. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Archive Expansion Detector practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Collection growth tracking over time (foundational)
description: Per-collection record counts are tracked across snapshots, and growth rates are computed as records per day. Collections growing faster than a threshold are flagged as expanding rapidly. Growth tracking distinguishes healthy expansion from runaway ingestion that might need review. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
hist = {'tools': [1000, 1200, 1500]}  # snapshots
rate = (hist['tools'][-1] - hist['tools'][0]) / 2
print('growth rate:', rate, 'records/day', '-> EXPANDING' if rate > 100 else '')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Archive Expansion Detector practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Resource catalog expansion scan (foundational)
description: Connected resource catalogs, such as tool and API registries, are scanned for new entries since the last snapshot. New resources are classified by type and linked to the databases they belong to. The scan keeps the system's map of available resources current. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
old_res, new_res = {'api1', 'api2'}, {'api2', 'api3'}
print('new resources:', sorted(new_res - old_res))
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Archive Expansion Detector practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Expansion report for operators (foundational)
description: Findings roll up into an expansion report: new databases with metadata, growth leaders, new resources, and unreachable flags. The report is the operator's morning briefing on what the archive gained overnight. It is diffed against the previous report so only changes demand attention. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
